preconditions.description: Input consists of integers n (number of nodes) and k (number of exit-nodes) within the specified bounds.

preconditions.expression: all(c.isdigit() for c in stdin.split() if c.isdigit())
preconditions.description: Input values are valid integers (no non-digit characters except whitespace).

postconditions.description: The first line of output is the minimum possible maximum distance between any two exit-nodes.

postconditions.expression: len(stdout.strip().split()) == (n - 1) * 2 + 1 and all(1 <= int(x) <= n for x in stdout.strip().split()[1:])
postconditions.description: The output contains exactly n-1 edges, each represented by two node IDs between 1 and n.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(x) <= n for x in stdout.strip().split()[1:]) and len(set(stdout.strip().split()[1:])) == 2 * (n - 1)
postconditions.description: Each edge is listed exactly once, and all node IDs are valid.

postconditions.expression: any(' '.join(map(str, edge)) in stdout.strip() for edge in [(i, j) for i in range(1, n + 1) for j in range(i + 1, n + 1)])
postconditions.description: The output contains a valid spanning tree with n-1 edges connecting all nodes.

postconditions.expression: len([x for x in range(1, n + 1) if sum(1 for edge in stdout.strip().split()[1:] if int(x) in edge) == 1]) == k
postconditions.description: Exactly k nodes have degree 1 (exit-nodes), and the rest have degree >= 2.

postconditions.expression: min_distance == int(stdout.strip().split()[0]) and all(max_distance_between_exits(input_graph) <= min_distance for input_graph in possible_graphs(n, k))
postconditions.description: The first line of output is the minimum possible maximum distance between any two exit-nodes in the constructed network.
